YOM-HOOKS(3) YOM User Manual YOM-HOOKS(3)

NAME

yom-hooks - lightweight hook API for the YOM shell

SYNOPSIS

hook HOOKED PATH

DESCRIPTION

The YOM-hook API allows you to replace YOM builtins with a specified binary. The following hooks are accepted: builtins, cd, core, echo, eval, exit, pwd, read.

HOW TO USE

To use hooks, write the command in a file and execute it with YOM:

hook <HOOKED> <PATH/TO/HOOK>

To target all builtins simultaneously, use the shortcut:

hook builtins <PATH/TO/HOOK>
The <PATH/TO/HOOK> parameter specifies the location of the hook binary. This path can start from the home directory (indicated by a tilde ~) or the root directory (indicated by a slash /).

To disable a hook and revert to the default behavior, run:

hook <HOOKED> default

Builtins

yom provides hooks for all of its builtins: builtins, cd, echo, exit, pwd, read. The builtins keyword is a shortcut that applies the hook to all available builtins.

Core Eval

The core hook is used to add an interactivity layer. The syntax is identical to other hooks:

hook core <PATH/TO/HOOK>
The eval hook uses the same syntax: 
hook eval <PATH/TO/HOOK>
The purpose of eval is to add new commands by evaluating the input string and either running it or exiting.

API

API Notes

All yom hooks pass their hook name as arg1 (using the lowercase names listed above).

cd

The cd hook passes the target directory as arg2 and pipes stdout. Simply write the full path of the destination directory to stdout. Full access to stdin and stderr is granted.

core

The core hook configures yom to act as a login shell. It requires you to bind to the following socket:

/tmp/yom_core.sock
Every time a user inputs a command, 
eval <COMMAND>
is sent down the socket, terminated by a newline. yom will then return one of two responses:
  • C followed by a newline if the directory has not changed.
  • :</path/to/new/directory/> followed by a newline to indicate a directory change.

Once the core process dies, yom cleans up the environment. The core hook only needs to exit when explicitly instructed by the user. Full access to stdin, stdout, and stderr is granted.

echo

The echo hook passes the string to be printed as arg2. It retains full access to stdin, stdout, and stderr.

err_write

The hook runs every time an error is to be recorded via the internal yom function, err_write. arg2 is the desired message to be printed (this is excluding all error: beggining text). Full access to stdout stderr and stdin is granted

eval

The eval hook runs at the beginning of every processing cycle. The hook name is passed as arg1, and the string to evaluate is passed as arg2. If the string matches an executable command, exit with code 0. Any other exit code indicates no match. Full access to standard I/O (stdin, stdout, and stderr) is granted.

exit

The exit hook receives the target exit code as arg2. The exit code returned by your hook will become the final shell exit code. Full access to stdin, stdout, and stderr is granted.

pwd

The pwd hook has full access to stdin, stdout, and stderr.

read

The read hook replaces the native read builtin. It should print the user-provided value directly to stdout. Full access to stdin and stderr is granted.
